/-!
# Erdős Problem 31

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/31](https://www.erdosproblems.com/31)
- [Er56] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in additive number theory*. Colloque sur la Théorie des
  Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
- [Er59] Erdős, P., *Über einige Probleme der additiven Zahlentheorie*. Sammelband zu Ehren des 250.
  Geburtstages Leonhard Eulers (1959), 116-119.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial
  theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
- [Lo54] Lorentz, G. G., *On a problem of additive number theory*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (1954), 838-841.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos31

open Filter
open scoped Pointwise

/--
Given any infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ there is a set $B$ of density $0$ such that $A+B$ contains all except finitely many integers.

Conjectured by Erdős and Straus. Proved by Lorentz [Lo54].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos31.lean"]
theorem erdos_31 : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite →
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, B.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B := by
  sorry

end Erdos31

reformulations.difference: The Lean quantifies over `A B : Set ℕ` with 0 ∈ ℕ allowed. The source (and Lorentz, as summarised on the erdosproblems forum) speaks of sets of positive integers. "All except finitely many integers" is written `∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B` over ℕ. "Density 0" is `Set.HasDensity B 0`, which counts B ∩ [0, b) against b.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (Lean ⇒ positive-integer version) Given an infinite A of positive integers, take the Lean B (it may contain 0) and shift it to B+1. B+1 consists of positive integers, still has density 0 (its counting function is at most B's), and A + (B+1) = (A+B)+1 contains every large n. (Positive-integer version ⇒ Lean) Given an infinite A ⊆ ℕ that may contain 0, apply the positive version to A \ {0}, which is still infinite; then A \ {0} + B ⊆ A + B. On ℕ, atTop equals cofinite, so `∀ᶠ n in atTop` means "all but finitely many". Counting from 0 rather than 1 changes the counting function by at most 1, which does not affect density 0. Proved in Lean as `erdos31_iff_pos` (standard axioms only): the repository's statement ↔ `∀ A, (∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) → A.Infinite → ∃ B, (∀ b ∈ B, 0 < b) ∧ B.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B`.

review.notes:
No defects found. The file has one declaration. Its statement matches erdosproblems.com/31 word for word in meaning, and the docstring repeats the source. Checks done in /workspace/review:
(1) Elaboration: `A + B` is the pointwise sumset (`Set.add`), and `HasDensity` is taken relative to `Set.univ`, i.e. natural density.
(2) Equivalence with the positive-integer reading, proved in Lean.
(3) Non-degeneracy tests: `univ` does not have density 0, `B = ∅` never works, and the easy case A = univ works with B = {0}.
(4) formal_proof: the linked theorem is `∃ B, HasDensity B 0 ∧ ∃ n0, ∀ n ≥ n0, n ∈ A + B`, with a verbatim local copy of `HasDensity`. I proved in Lean that it implies the repository statement and vice versa. The linked file has no `sorry`. The linked v4.29.1 copy targets Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1 and does not build against this repo's v4.33.1, only because of Mathlib API drift (e.g. an unknown lemma name). The same repository's v4.33.0 copy (src/latest), with the identical final theorem, builds here with no errors, and `#print axioms` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
The link points at a `main`-branch path rather than a fixed commit. About 80 other files in the repo do the same, so I did not treat it as a defect; pinning a commit would make it more stable.
Status is consistent: the file says `research solved` with a lean4 formal_proof, and the source says \"PROVED (LEAN)\".
Lorentz's original paper (AMS) and the Erdős papers could not be downloaded because of Cloudflare. The forum comment on erdosproblems.com states Lorentz's stronger quantitative theorem, B(n) ≤ C Σ_{k≤n} log A(k)/A(k), which implies the density-0 claim. The page numbers it quotes fall inside the page ranges the file gives.
